instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice in a pot until the water runs mostly clear. Add 2 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch pieces. Cut the eggplants into 1-inch pieces on an angle. Cut the peppers into 1-inch pieces. Cook the potatoes and eggplants soon after cutting.
Smash and peel the garlic cloves. Slice the green onions. Stir 1 tbsp cornstarch into 3 tbsp water in a small bowl.
In another small bowl, stir together 2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp white pepper and the sesame oil.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the potatoes in a single layer and cook for 12 minutes, stirring every minute or two, until golden and a knife slides in easily.
Add the peppers and cook for 1 minute. Transfer the potatoes and peppers to a large plate.

Add 2 tbsp oil to the same pan and turn the heat to medium-high. Add half the eggplant in a single layer. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then and covering the pan for 1 minute at a time, until browned and soft. Transfer it to the plate.
Add 2 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the eggplant the same way.
Turn the heat to medium-low and add the garlic. Stir for 10 seconds, until you can smell it.
Return all the vegetables to the pan and pour in the sauce. Turn the heat to high and stir for 30 seconds.
Stir the cornstarch mixture again and pour it in, then add most of the green onions. Stir for 30 seconds, until the sauce turns glossy and coats everything.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice and the remaining green onions on top.
method_notes: The lead and the other versions agree on the method: cook the potato first, the pepper briefly, and the eggplant in between, then bring them together in a light garlic soy sauce thickened with cornstarch. They differ on frying: one deep fries, one coats the eggplant in cornstarch and soaks it in salt water, and the lead pan-fries in a few tablespoons of oil, which is what this does. Quantities are scaled from the lead's 2 servings to 4 with green peppers as the dish is named, and the lead's rating is the page's visible 4.80 from 45 votes.
